This report explains the KC model that all later steps use. Report 07 takes the same model and pins it to the recordings. Here it runs in its prediction form, set up before the recordings arrived: 20% of KCs respond to an odor (averaged over odors) with APL blocked, and 10% with APL intact. Every symbol is defined in Table 1, and again where it first appears.

The model in one paragraph

Each KC adds up its claws' glomerular inputs (a weighted average of the glomeruli's odor responses, with weights from the connectome). It responds by how much that sum exceeds a threshold. APL is one cell whose activity, for each odor, is the average response of the KCs. It inhibits every KC by subtracting a fixed multiple of that activity. Because APL's activity depends on the KC responses and the KC responses depend on APL's activity, both are solved together for each odor ("self-consistently"). "Blocked" (TNT) means no APL at all. Later versions replace the uniform APL with connectome measurements of where APL's synapses are.

1What the model is

The model is a rate model of the calyx. A rate model describes each cell by one number per odor (its response), not by spikes or a time course. There is one model per mushroom body: hemibrain R, male CNS L and male CNS R. FlyWire and BANC were dropped on 2026-10-21 at Yang's request. Figure 1 shows the circuit and where each symbol acts.

2Step 1: one model per mushroom body

The hemibrain contains one calyx, the right one (1,793 KCs with claws). The male CNS contains both. Its KCs are split into left and right in two steps. First, each KC's position is the mean of its claw centroids. Second, two-means clustering (k-means with k=2k = 2k=2, seed 0) on those positions gives two groups. Each group is named after the APL that its KCs' on-claw APL synapses mostly contact (APL_L or APL_R). This gives 1,876 KCs on the left and 1,900 on the right (Figure 2). Each mushroom body gets its own WWW, uuu, vvv and threshold, and its own calibrated gains. Results are averaged over the three only at the end.

3Step 2: input weights from the claws

A claw is a cluster of one KC's postsynaptic sites from antennal-lobe PNs in the calyx. Sites within 2 µm of each other (single linkage) belong to the same claw. Report 02 describes how claws are found. Each claw is assigned to one glomerulus, the glomerulus of its main PN (the PN that makes most of the claw's PN synapses), and all its PN synapses count for that glomerulus. Only uniglomerular PN types count. Claws whose main PN is multiglomerular, bi-glomerular or untyped stay in the denominator but give no input. The input weight is

Wkg  =  ∑c ∈ claws(k): g(c)=gnc∑c ∈ claws(k)nc(1)W_{kg} \;=\; \frac{\displaystyle\sum_{c \,\in\, \mathrm{claws}(k):\ g(c)=g} n_c}{\displaystyle\sum_{c \,\in\, \mathrm{claws}(k)} n_c} \tag{1}Wkg​=c∈claws(k)∑​nc​c∈claws(k): g(c)=g∑​nc​​(1)
ncn_cnc​ = PN synapses on claw ccc; the sum on top runs over KC kkk's claws of glomerulus ggg, the sum below over all its claws

The drive of KC kkk by odor ooo is the WWW-weighted sum of its glomeruli's responses:

xko  =  ∑gWkg  rgo(2)x_{ko} \;=\; \sum_g W_{kg}\; r_{go} \tag{2}xko​=g∑​Wkg​rgo​(2)

Because the weights of one KC add up to at most 1, xkox_{ko}xko​ is a weighted average of the responses of the KC's glomeruli. Claws of glomeruli outside the response table count as 0. The drive is therefore smaller for KCs whose claws come mostly from unmeasured glomeruli.

4Step 3: odor input to the glomeruli

Two tables give rgor_{go}rgo​, the response of glomerulus ggg to odor ooo. The model takes no PN-level transformation: these numbers go straight into Equation 2. Negative responses (inhibition below baseline) are set to 0.

  • ORN table (Yang's ORN_ovlp16_resp_flyave_merge_dropna.csv): 36 glomeruli × 16 odors, fly-averaged olfactory receptor neuron (ORN) responses. The file does not state units; the values behave like ΔF/F (range −0.19 to 2.07). Glomeruli in this table carry 76%–77% of the KCs' claw PN synapses (mean over KCs, per mushroom body).
  • GH146 table: mean peak ΔF/F of GH146 PNs (7 flies), 29 glomeruli × 13 odors. -aPine, euc and B-myr are missing, and paa comes from the diagnostics panel at 10⁻⁵ because it is the only PAA presentation. These glomeruli carry 63%–64% of the claw PN synapses.

5Step 4: KC drive and the threshold with APL blocked

With APL blocked there is no inhibition, so a KC responds by how far its drive exceeds the threshold θ\thetaθ:

ykoblocked  =  [ xko−θ ]+where [z]+=max⁡(z,0)(3)y^{\mathrm{blocked}}_{ko} \;=\; \left[\, x_{ko} - \theta \,\right]_+ \qquad \text{where } [z]_+ = \max(z, 0) \tag{3}ykoblocked​=[xko​−θ]+​where [z]+​=max(z,0)(3)

θ\thetaθ is one number per mushroom body and input table. It is found by bisection so that, averaged over odors, 20% of KCs respond (yko>0y_{ko} > 0yko​>0). The bisection keeps an interval [θlo,θhi][\theta_{lo}, \theta_{hi}][θlo​,θhi​], which starts at 0 and the largest drive. At each step it tests the midpoint: if more than 20% respond there, the threshold must be higher, so the midpoint becomes θlo\theta_{lo}θlo​; otherwise it becomes θhi\theta_{hi}θhi​. 60 halvings make the interval negligibly small. Individual odors then respond at different levels (Figure 5). Strong odors drive many KCs past the shared threshold, and weak ones drive few.

6Step 5: APL feedback and what "solved self-consistently" means

With APL intact, each KC is inhibited in proportion to APL's activity for that odor:

yko  =  [ xko−θ−a uk Ao ]+(5)y_{ko} \;=\; \left[\, x_{ko} - \theta - a\, u_k\, A_o \,\right]_+ \tag{5}yko​=[xko​−θ−auk​Ao​]+​(5)

and APL's activity is the mean response of the KCs, each weighted by how strongly it drives APL:

Ao  =  1N∑k=1Nvk yko(6)A_o \;=\; \frac{1}{N}\sum_{k=1}^{N} v_k\, y_{ko} \tag{6}Ao​=N1​k=1∑N​vk​yko​(6)

In the uniform version (U) every uk=vk=1u_k = v_k = 1uk​=vk​=1. Every KC then gets the same inhibition aAoa A_oaAo​ for a given odor, and APL's activity is simply the mean KC response. The gain aaa is one number per mushroom body and version. It is the same for every odor and every KC. The inhibition still differs between odors, because AoA_oAo​ does.

Why "self-consistently"

AoA_oAo​ appears on both sides. The KC responses (Equation 5) depend on APL's activity, and APL's activity (Equation 6) depends on the KC responses. The model needs the one value of AoA_oAo​ that reproduces itself: the value that, when used to compute the KC responses, gives back the same AoA_oAo​ as their mean. Mathematically this is a fixed point. Physically, it is the steady state in which APL and the KCs have settled.

To find it, define for each odor the function

Fo(A)  =  1N∑kvk[ xko−θ−a uk A ]+(7)F_o(A) \;=\; \frac{1}{N}\sum_{k} v_k \left[\, x_{ko} - \theta - a\, u_k\, A \,\right]_+ \tag{7}Fo​(A)=N1​k∑​vk​[xko​−θ−auk​A]+​(7)
the APL activity the KCs would produce if APL's activity were AAA

and solve A=Fo(A)A = F_o(A)A=Fo​(A). FoF_oFo​ starts at Fo(0)F_o(0)Fo​(0), the mean (weighted) response with no inhibition, and can only fall as AAA grows, because more inhibition never raises a KC's response. The line AAA rises from 0. The two cross exactly once, which makes the solution unique (Figure 6). The code finds it by bisection on [0,Fo(0)][0, F_o(0)][0,Fo​(0)]: if A>Fo(A)A > F_o(A)A>Fo​(A) at the midpoint, the crossing lies below it; otherwise above. 60 halvings, done for all odors at once (function fixed_point in apl_block_model.py).

7Step 6: calibrating the APL gain

The gain aaa sets how strong APL is. It is chosen so that, with APL intact, 10% of KCs respond on average over odors, half the blocked level. More gain means more inhibition and fewer KCs responding, so the mean fraction falls steadily as aaa grows. The code (function calib) starts at a=1a = 1a=1 and doubles it until the fraction drops to 10% or below. It then bisects 50 times between the last two values. Every evaluation solves the fixed point of Step 5 for all odors.

8Step 7: what is read out

Three quantities are read out for every mushroom body, version and input table:

  • Fraction responding per odor, ϕo\phi_oϕo​, blocked and intact.
  • Odor-pair similarity SabS_{ab}Sab​: the cosine similarity of the two odors' KC population response vectors ya=(y1a,…,yNa)\mathbf{y}_a = (y_{1a}, \dots, y_{Na})ya​=(y1a​,…,yNa​) and yb\mathbf{y}_byb​ (Equation 8). It is the same measure as Yang's RDMs (which hold 1−S1 - S1−S). Because responses are ≥ 0, SSS runs from 0 (no KC responds to both) to 1 (the same pattern up to a scale factor). It is undefined when an odor drives no KC.
  • The effect of blocking APL on a pair, ΔSab=Sabblocked−Sabintact\Delta S_{ab} = S^{\mathrm{blocked}}_{ab} - S^{\mathrm{intact}}_{ab}ΔSab​=Sabblocked​−Sabintact​ (Equation 9). It is computed per mushroom body and then averaged over the three.
Sab  =  cos⁡(ya,yb)  =  ∑kyka ykb∑kyka2  ∑kykb2(8)S_{ab} \;=\; \cos(\mathbf{y}_a, \mathbf{y}_b) \;=\; \frac{\sum_k y_{ka}\, y_{kb}}{\sqrt{\sum_k y_{ka}^2}\;\sqrt{\sum_k y_{kb}^2}} \tag{8}Sab​=cos(ya​,yb​)=∑k​yka2​​∑k​ykb2​​∑k​yka​ykb​​(8)
ΔSab  =  Sabblocked−Sabintact(9)\Delta S_{ab} \;=\; S^{\mathrm{blocked}}_{ab} - S^{\mathrm{intact}}_{ab} \tag{9}ΔSab​=Sabblocked​−Sabintact​(9)

Odors that drive fewer than 0.5% of KCs with APL intact (in any version and mushroom body) are left out of the pair results, because their similarity rests on a handful of KCs. In the main setting this drops ms with ORN input and none with GH146 input.

9Step 8: versions that use APL's connectome wiring

Each version replaces part of the uniform APL with a connectome measurement. All of them keep the same blocked responses and the same θ, and all are calibrated to the same 10%. The versions therefore differ only in where the inhibition acts and how it is weighted. Table 6 summarizes them.

9.1C: APL synapses per KC

uku_kuk​ is KC kkk's number of APL→KC synapses in the calyx, divided by the mean over the mushroom body's KCs. vkv_kvk​ is the same for KC→APL synapses (calyx only since 2026-10-21, at Yang's request). A KC with uk=2u_k = 2uk​=2 receives twice the average inhibition for the same APL activity, and a KC with vk=2v_k = 2vk​=2 counts twice as much toward APL's activity. APL is still one unit with one activity per odor. The two controls ask whether it matters which KC has which counts (Cs keeps each KC class's distribution but shuffles it) or only the class averages (Cc).

9.2P, L, M: APL synapses per glomerulus

In P and L, inhibition divides a glomerulus's input instead of subtracting from the KC, because APL→PN synapses act presynaptically on the PN boutons and scale down what the boutons pass to all their KCs. pgp_gpg​ (P) is the number of APL→PN synapses on glomerulus ggg's boutons per PN→KC synapse of those boutons. qgq_gqg​ (L) is the number of APL→KC synapses on ggg's claws per PN synapse on those claws. Report 04 shows both across glomeruli. Within each mushroom body, the weights are scaled so that their claw-input-weighted mean is 1:

p~g  =  pg(∑g′wg′ pg′)/∑g′wg′,wg=∑kWkg(10)\tilde p_g \;=\; \frac{p_g}{\left(\sum_{g'} w_{g'}\, p_{g'}\right) \big/ \sum_{g'} w_{g'}}, \qquad w_g = \sum_k W_{kg} \tag{10}p~​g​=(∑g′​wg′​pg′​)/∑g′​wg′​pg​​,wg​=k∑​Wkg​(10)
sums over glomeruli g′g'g′ that have a value; glomeruli without a value get p~g=1\tilde p_g = 1p~​g​=1

With this scaling, P and P0 put the same total inhibition on the average claw input, and only its distribution across glomeruli differs. In M0 and M only a share fff of the inhibition goes to boutons. fff = APL→PN ÷ (APL→PN + APL→KC) synapses in the calyx, 0.097 in hemibrain and 0.112 in male CNS. The rest is uniform on the KCs. The KC gain is (1−f) aU(1-f)\,a_U(1−f)aU​, the bouton gain f bP0f\,b_{P0}fbP0​, and both are scaled by one common factor sss to reach 10%.

10Results of the prediction run

  • Uniform APL. The KCs gained by blocking APL track odor strength (r = 0.99 with ORN input), and so do all versions (r ≥ 0.999 between versions). Similarity rises most for pairs of strong odors: mean ΔS\Delta SΔS +0.076 with ORN and +0.041 with GH146. The pattern is the same in all three mushroom bodies (median r between them 0.87 and 0.81).
  • Per-KC counts (C). They change ΔS\Delta SΔS by 0.029 on average (ORN), but the same counts shuffled within class do much the same (maps r 0.72). What is left differs between mushroom bodies (median r 0.34).
  • Boutons per glomerulus (P vs P0). A consistent pattern (median r 0.87 between mushroom bodies; mean |change| 0.034): pa–eb and pa–ep rise more, eb and ep move away from 1-6ol and 1-8ol.
  • At the boutons' real share (M vs M0) the same pattern shrinks to a mean |change| of 0.006.
  • Claws (L vs P0): mean |change| 0.018.
What this step does not include

One threshold for all KCs, with no differences in excitability between classes, and no spikes or time course.

APL is one unit with one activity per odor in every version. P and L weight its output per glomerulus but do not make its activity local. A local, non-spiking APL is modelled separately (scripts/apl_local_model.py).

The inputs are ORN or GH146 averages from other flies, not the recorded flies' PNs.

The coding levels (20% blocked, 10% intact) are assumptions here. Report 07 replaces them with the recordings.
